claim.binary_failure_condition: The dispute deadline or business-day count is wrong, the filing and dispute clocks are conflated, an unsupported filing time is added, or a required action, owner, deadline, or precise locator is missing or incorrect.
claim.binary_pass_condition: The workpaper computes the dispute deadline using the five-business-day contract clock, keeps the annual filing date as a separate regulatory control without inventing a filing time, and states the required notice or follow-up actions with correct owners and precise locators.
candidate_evidence_requirements: An action register and decision-summary section showing action, responsible owner, governing source, deadline, and precise locator for both commercial response and filing readiness.
claim.description: The decision summary distinguishes the contract dispute response from annual compliance filing readiness and assigns each action a responsible owner and governing deadline.
claim.independent_failure_mode: All quantities and amounts can be correct while the notice schedule or separation of contractual and regulatory clocks is independently wrong.
claim.title: Commercial and filing actions have correct clocks

entities.description: Fictional Massachusetts competitive supplier buying Class I certificates.
Fictional bilateral seller responsible for delivery and cure.
Executed confirmation and its cure-and-cover amendment.
Frozen public authority controlling eligibility and filing interfaces.

route_context.business_goal: Close the seller's 2024 Class I delivery without paying for unusable certificates and preserve a supportable compliance inventory.
route_context.deliverable_class: Auditable certificate-delivery settlement workbook with embedded procurement and accounting decision summary
difficulty_sources: Temporal qualification and lifecycle precedence across different systems
Pixel-essential reversal and overlap evidence whose raw baselines and dimension-preserved annotations traverse two independently auditable PDF-to-DOCX chains
Visual trade-to-allocation-to-registry custody handoff that separates executed cover damages from buyer-held compliance inventory
As-of qualification-exception event precedence after exact unit authority matching and before downstream settlement propagation
route_context.natural_request_context: A settlement manager needs a single spreadsheet workpaper for the procurement director and controller after the final tender arrived on June 9.
route_context.terminal_decision: After admitting the reversal and overlap only from the two raw-plus-marked cross-document evidence pairs, approve USD 16,920 net payable; post 950 seller RECs and 40 cover RECs separately; dispute 50 seller RECs, record a 10-REC residual shortfall, send dispute by June 16, and preserve July 1 filing readiness.
route_context.unique_resolution: Exact source precedence, inclusive serial arithmetic, lifecycle event order, signed cure hierarchy, cover execution, paired raw/derived lineage admissibility, and conservation equations admit only the stated quantities, payable, and deadlines. The cover inventory component additionally requires an exact trade-to-allocation-to-final-registry-custody match by the cutoff; absent that final handoff, the cover posting is zero and the residual is fifty while the damage offset remains unchanged. The otherwise valid LOT-D unit must additionally have QX-38983-2025 in a final released state by noon; a pending, late, or mismatched release withholds its 150 certificates from the close and forces the stated downstream quantity, payable, inventory, and residual counterfactual.

rules.counterexample: Using July 1 as the invoice dispute deadline fails.
rules.resolution_order: Contract clock first for dispute; regulation independently for filing.
rules.statement: The buyer's five-business-day dispute clock starts on the first business day after final tender and excludes weekends, yielding June 16 at 17:00 EDT; regulatory filing remains July 1.
truth_conditions: June 10, 11, 12, 13, and 16 are the five counted business days.

state_facts.interpretation: This is the scenario trigger, not the regulatory filing deadline.
state_facts.materialization_obligation: Delivery statement and intake record must show this timestamp.

state_facts.interpretation: Five business days run from the next business day after June 9.
state_facts.materialization_obligation: Contract business-day clause and June close calendar must uniquely yield this deadline.

state_facts.interpretation: The authority fixes the filing date, not a 17:00 time; it is separate from contract dispute timing.
state_facts.materialization_obligation: Regulation and close calendar must identify July 1, 2025 for CY2024 without attributing an unstated time of day to DOER.

citations.observation: The dispute action is owned and due June 16 at 17:00 after a five-business-day computation, while the separate compliance action is owned by Compliance and due July 1 with no invented time.

reference_claim_evidence.why_full_pass: Commercial and regulatory clocks, governing sources, owners, notices, residual follow-up, and filing-readiness outputs are all distinguished and precisely sourced.
